transcript: Jonathan Groff giving stellar leading performances in back to back Broadway seasons shouldn't be a surprise to anyone, but that makes it no less impressive. In Just In Time, a new musical developed and directed by Alex Timbers, Jonathan Groff takes us through the fast and furious life of Bobby Darin. Flanked by an on-stage band and swaggering across an immersive nightclub setting, he exemplifies a remarkable aptitude for crowd work. The supporting actors make great use of their stage time as well, especially Gracie Lawrence who is giving an incredible vocal performance as Connie Francis and leaves you wanting more. The efficient staging is perfectly tailored to this particular set, and it feels fresh and alive. The nightclub experience totally hits and there's no bad seat in the house. Even if you don't know a thing about Bobby Darin or his music, you'll be hard-pressed to not have a good time here. That said, you might leave the show still not knowing all that much about Bobby Darin himself. The glossiness of this production and the amazing performance by Jonathan Groff does a very good job of distracting from the fact that the show falls into some of the common jukebox musical tropes — mainly that it's a bit predictable and that the story is event-driven more than it is character-driven. There are hints of complexity in Bobby Darin's true character, the person underneath the persona, but there's little to no focus on digging into the psychology of this human being. The show kind of overwhelms you with singing, dancing, lights, atmosphere, the works — to the point where you don't really have time to be wondering about this. It’s just something I thought about in retrospect. I'm not convinced that this show will stick much with me in a year's time, for example, but much like Bobby Darin's life, it was beautifully ephemeral and exciting. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer recommends the show despite acknowledging significant flaws, praising Groff's performance and the nightclub experience while noting the shallow character development and predictable plot typical of jukebox musicals.
